newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's cabinet approves 1997 budget draft.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's cabinet approves 1997 budget draft.

text.p: Portugal's cabinet approved a draft of 1997 budget proposals that include a forecast that the budget deficit will drop to 2.9 percent of gross domestic product and no tax rises, Presidency Minister Antonio Vitorino said.
"This proposal foresees a reduction in the budget deficit to 2.9 percent of GDP in 1997," Vitorino told reporters.
The government expects the budget deficit in 1996 to stand at around four percent.
The Socialist government of Prime Minister Antonio Guterres plans to present its 1997 budget proposals to parliament on October 15. Analysts expect the budget to be passed in November.
"The budget aims to continue the reduction of public debt in relation to GDP," Vitorino said.
"There will not be increases in direct or indirect taxes (in 1997)," he said.
"The budget will give priority to public investment and the rigorous containment of current spending," he added.
The draft budget proposals will be presented to opposition political parties on Friday for discussion, Vitorino said.
